name: Email Bombing
summary: Adversaries may flood targeted email addresses with an overwhelming volume of messages. This may bury legitimate emails in a flood of spam and disrupt business operations. An adversary may accomplish email bombing by leveraging an automated bot to register a targeted address for e-mail lists that do not validate new signups, such as online newsletters. analytics.name: Analytic 1008
analytics.guidance: Detect abnormally high volume of inbound email messages or repetitive attachments being delivered to a single mailbox within a short time window. Defenders should look for anomalous spikes in message counts and repetitive attachment file creation events correlated with targeted users.

analytics.name: Analytic 1009
analytics.guidance: Monitor mail server logs (e.g., Postfix, Sendmail) for excessive connections or inbound message counts targeting a single recipient. Correlate with repetitive attachment storage in /var/mail or /var/spool/mail directories.

analytics.name: Analytic 1010
analytics.guidance: Detect abnormal use of email clients (e.g., Outlook, Thunderbird) showing mass arrival of messages or repetitive attachments being locally stored. Correlate message volume with file creation activity in mail cache directories.

analytics.name: Analytic 1011
analytics.guidance: Monitor unified logs and Mail.app activity for repetitive incoming messages with attachments. Defenders should look for large volumes of incoming mail stored under ~/Library/Mail with unusual timing or repetitive subjects.
